name: Alonso Mudarra
description: Alonso Mudarra was a Spanish priest and composer who helped shape the repertory of the vihuela and early guitar. His 1546 collection includes instrumental fantasias, dances and intabulations as well as songs in Spanish, Latin and Italian. The collection is an important witness to the expressive range of plucked-string music in Renaissance Spain.

name: Francisco Guerrero
description: Francisco Guerrero was one of the leading Spanish Renaissance composers, celebrated for sacred music of warmth, clarity and devotional intensity. His career was centred on Seville Cathedral, though his music circulated widely across Europe and the Americas. He wrote masses, motets, passions and vernacular devotional works.

name: Sebastián Aguilera de Heredia
description: Sebastián Aguilera de Heredia was a Spanish organist and composer whose keyboard works stand at the transition from Renaissance counterpoint to the more idiomatic Baroque organ style. His tientos and other pieces combine intricate imitation with bold harmonic turns and rhythmic vitality, contributing to the distinctive Iberian organ tradition.

ORGAN MUSIC
Tientos

Magnificat settings

name: Jan Dismas Zelenka
description: Jan Dismas Zelenka was a Bohemian composer who spent most of his career in Dresden. His music is distinguished by daring harmony, intricate counterpoint, rhythmic invention and a highly individual treatment of sacred forms. Long overshadowed by better-known contemporaries, he is now recognised as one of the most original composers of the late Baroque.

name: Élisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre
description: Élisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre was a French harpsichordist and composer admired at the court of Louis XIV. Her output spans harpsichord suites, trio sonatas, cantatas and opera, displaying contrapuntal skill alongside dramatic sensitivity. She was among the most accomplished women composers of the French Baroque.

name: Isabella Leonarda
description: Isabella Leonarda was an Italian nun and one of the most prolific women composers of the seventeenth century. Her large body of sacred vocal music includes motets, masses and concerted works. Her Opus 16 sonatas are among the earliest instrumental sonatas published by a woman, demonstrating her command of emerging Baroque forms.

name: Chiara Margarita Cozzolani
description: Chiara Margarita Cozzolani was an Italian Benedictine nun and composer in Milan. Her sacred music makes vivid use of solo voices, duets, choirs and basso continuo, combining expressive text setting with the concerted style of the early Baroque. Her surviving publications reveal the sophisticated musical life of convents in seventeenth-century Italy.

name: Antonia Bembo
description: Antonia Bembo was a Venetian singer and composer who settled in France and received support from Louis XIV. Her surviving collection Produzioni armoniche contains vocal and instrumental music of considerable scale, including sacred works and operatic writing. Her career offers a striking example of a woman composer building an independent artistic life abroad.

name: Johann Christoph Pepusch
description: Johann Christoph Pepusch was a German-born composer and theorist who became an influential figure in London's musical life. He worked across instrumental and vocal genres and is best known today for arranging the music for John Gay's The Beggar's Opera. His career reflects the cosmopolitan exchange between continental and British musical cultures.

name: Francesco Bartolomeo Conti
description: Francesco Bartolomeo Conti was an Italian composer and theorbo player active at the imperial court in Vienna. He composed operas, serenatas, oratorios and instrumental music, contributing to the cosmopolitan theatrical culture of the Habsburg court. His works show the interaction of Italian vocal traditions with Viennese courtly taste.

name: Francesco Mancini
description: Francesco Mancini was a Neapolitan composer and organist associated with the flourishing musical institutions of Naples. His output includes operas, sacred vocal music and instrumental works, especially concertos and sonatas for recorder and flute. His writing is valuable for understanding the Neapolitan style between Corelli's generation and the Classical era.

name: Hélène de Montgeroult
description: Hélène de Montgeroult was a French pianist, composer and influential piano pedagogue whose music bridges Classical form and early Romantic expression. Her extensive piano method contains original studies that combine technical instruction with sophisticated musical writing. Her career challenges the notion that major developments in piano composition were made only by men.

name: Josepha Barbara Auernhammer
description: Josepha Barbara Auernhammer was an Austrian pianist, teacher and composer who studied with Mozart and performed his works with him. Her compositions include piano sonatas, variations and chamber music, reflecting the virtuoso keyboard culture of Vienna in the late eighteenth century. She was an important musical professional in her own right.

name: Marianna Auenbrugger
description: Marianna Auenbrugger was an Austrian pianist and composer praised by Joseph Haydn. She died at twenty-two, leaving a small but significant trace of the musical culture of late eighteenth-century Vienna. Her story also illuminates the barriers facing women composers whose work was rarely published or preserved.

name: Maria Hester Park
description: Maria Hester Park was an English composer, pianist and teacher active in London's concert life. She published sonatas, variations and other keyboard works, as well as vocal music. Her career represents the growing professional presence of women composers in Britain's public musical culture around 1800.

name: Joseph Martin Kraus
description: Joseph Martin Kraus was a German-born composer who made his career in Sweden, where he became a leading musical figure at the court of Gustav III. His symphonies and stage works combine Classical architecture with dramatic contrasts and a distinctive expressive intensity. His music deserves to be heard beyond the convenient but limiting label of 'the Swedish Mozart'.

description: Antonio Rosetti, born Anton Rösler, was a Bohemian-German composer whose career took him through German courts, including Wallerstein. He wrote symphonies, concertos, chamber works and sacred music, with particular flair for wind instruments. His output illustrates the richness of the Classical period beyond its most famous Viennese names.

name: Emilie Mayer
description: Emilie Mayer was a German composer whose substantial output includes eight symphonies, concert overtures, chamber music and piano works. She pursued a professional career in a period when women composers faced significant institutional barriers. Her music combines Classical formal discipline with the dramatic energy of nineteenth-century Romanticism.

name: Dora Pejačević
description: Dora Pejačević was a Croatian composer whose music moves from late Romantic richness toward a more modern, harmonically adventurous language. Her output includes a symphony, concertos, songs and chamber music. Long neglected after her early death, she is now recognised as a major figure in Croatian music history.

name: Louise Héritte-Viardot
description: Louise Héritte-Viardot was a French composer, pianist, singer and teacher, daughter of Pauline Viardot and niece of Maria Malibran. She wrote operas, orchestral and chamber music, as well as songs, and worked to establish a serious compositional career within a celebrated musical family. Much of her output remains insufficiently known.

description: Joachim Raff was a Swiss-born composer who became one of the most prolific symphonists of the nineteenth century. Initially associated with Liszt's circle, he developed a personal style combining clear Classical structures with Romantic colour and thematic invention. His large catalogue includes symphonies, concertos, chamber music and operas.

name: Friedrich von Flotow
description: Friedrich von Flotow was a German composer best known for his operas, especially Martha, which enjoyed international popularity in the nineteenth century. Educated partly in Paris, he absorbed French opéra-comique and Italianate lyricism. His theatrical success made him a prominent figure in European opera, even as later repertory narrowed to a few works.

name: Manuel de Falla
description: Manuel de Falla was one of the central figures of twentieth-century Spanish music. He combined close study of Spanish song and dance with influences from French modernism, creating music of precision, colour and concentrated expression. His stage works, ballets and chamber pieces helped establish a distinctive modern Spanish musical language.

name: Joaquín Turina
description: Joaquín Turina was a Spanish composer and pianist whose style combines French-influenced harmonic colour with Andalusian rhythms and melodic gestures. After studying in Paris, he became a leading voice in the musical revival of early twentieth-century Spain. His output ranges from orchestral works to chamber music, piano pieces and songs.

name: Joaquín Rodrigo
description: Joaquín Rodrigo was a Spanish composer whose concertos helped establish the modern classical guitar as a major solo instrument with orchestra. Blind from early childhood, he developed a refined style drawing on Spanish historical and folk traditions without simply reproducing them. His music also includes songs, piano pieces and orchestral works.

name: Rebecca Saunders
description: Rebecca Saunders is a British composer whose music explores timbre, resonance, physical gesture and the spatial behaviour of sound. Her works often focus intensely on individual instruments or small ensembles, treating instrumental colour as a structural force. She is one of the most distinctive voices in contemporary European composition.

name: Olga Neuwirth
description: Olga Neuwirth is an Austrian composer whose work crosses instrumental composition, electronics, film, theatre and multimedia. Her music often challenges conventional concert forms and explores political memory, identity and the instability of perception. She is a leading figure in contemporary music theatre and experimental orchestral writing.

description: Joan Tower is an American composer and pianist known for energetic rhythms, vivid orchestral colour and a strong sense of instrumental character. name: Tania León
description: Tania León is a Cuban-born American composer and conductor whose work draws on Afro-Cuban rhythmic traditions, modernist techniques and a broad international outlook. Her compositions range from chamber music to opera and orchestral works. She has also been an influential advocate for new music and cultural exchange.

name: Julia Wolfe
description: Julia Wolfe is an American composer and co-founder of Bang on a Can. Her music combines the repetitive propulsion of minimalism with the force and textures of rock, folk and industrial sound. She often works with large ensembles and explores labour, history and collective experience through powerful, physically charged scores.

name: Chaya Czernowin
description: Chaya Czernowin is an Israeli-American composer whose music investigates the fragile boundaries between sound, noise, silence and perception. Her works often use extended instrumental techniques and unusual sonic relationships to create intensely physical listening experiences. She has become an influential voice in contemporary opera and instrumental composition.

description: Hans Abrahamsen is a Danish composer whose music moves from early New Simplicity toward a highly individual world of suspended time, delicate orchestration and transformed musical memory. His works often combine apparent clarity with subtle rhythmic and harmonic dislocation. His vocal and orchestral music has received wide international recognition.

His distinctive 'infinity series' generated intricate melodic and rhythmic structures, while his later works embraced startling contrasts and an almost organic sense of growth. He was one of the most influential Scandinavian composers of his generation.

description: Isang Yun was a Korean-born composer who developed an influential career in Germany. His music combines contemporary European techniques with ideas drawn from Korean musical traditions, especially the shaping and ornamentation of sustained tones. His work also reflects the political history of Korea and his own experience of imprisonment and exile.

Chen's career is closely connected with the development of modern orchestral music in China.
